subject: Business Models
title: Music Royalties
description: A quick, practical guide to Music Royalties.

hook.text: Every time a song plays on Spotify, the rights holder earns $0.003-$0.005 per stream.

buildup.text: Royalties flow to songwriters, performers, producers, and publishers—split according to contracts.

discovery.text: Investors now buy music catalogs as assets. Hipgnosis paid $300 million for Shakira's catalog alone.

twist.text: Most musicians earn almost nothing from streaming. The top 1% of artists capture 90% of revenue.

climax.text: Music royalties show how IP can generate passive income for decades after creation.

punchline.text: Write one hit song, earn royalties for life. IP pays forever.

quiz.question: Why are investors buying music catalogs?

details.summary: Music royalties are payments made each time a song is played, performed, or reproduced. Streaming services pay per-stream royalties averaging $0.003-0.005 to rights holders. Performance royalties come from radio, venues, and public spaces. Mechanical royalties come from recording reproductions.
details.whyItMatters: Music royalties represent a complex revenue model where a single creation generates income across dozens of channels for decades. Understanding royalty structures reveals how creative industries monetize intellectual property in the digital era.
takeaways: Songs earn royalties from streaming, radio, performance, and reproduction
Per-stream rates average fractions of a cent across major platforms
Royalty rights are split between songwriters, performers, labels, and publishers

faq.question: How are music streaming royalties calculated and distributed?
faq.answer: Spotify pools all subscription revenue, keeps roughly 30%, and distributes 70% to rights holders proportional to their share of total streams. A song getting 0.01% of all streams receives 0.01% of the royalty pool. This means per-stream rates fluctuate based on total platform activity.

faq.question: Why do many musicians earn so little from streaming royalties?
faq.answer: Per-stream rates are fractions of a cent. A million streams might earn $3,000-5,000, which is then split between the artist, songwriter, label, and publisher. Independent artists keep more per stream but have fewer streams. The model favors a small number of mega-popular artists.
